les: Wat ons van ons voorouers erf
kaps_punt: Wat is erfenis - 2 uur; en: Erfenis in voorwerpe: Voorbeeld: Goue voorwerpe by Mapungubwe: Limpopo

items.bewering: Erfenis is dinge en gewoontes wat ons uit die verlede ontvang, bewaar en aan die volgende geslagte oordra.
items.bron: Standard definition: heritage is 'an inheritance of both tangible and intangible goods from the past, preserved in the present and passed on to societies in the future' (IOL, Unathi Funde, Heritage Day article); the World Heritage Convention's purpose is to 'protect, conserve, present and transmit' heritage 'to future generations' (whc.unesco.org, Understanding World Heritage). 'Dinge en gewoontes' maps to tangible and intangible.

items.bewering: Ons ryk erfenis kom uit baie kulture en behoort aan almal in ons land.
items.bron: National Heritage Council, 'Our Heritage' (nhc.org.za): quotes Mandela on why Heritage Day became a national day, 'our rich and varied cultural heritage has a profound power to help build our new nation'. This is a value statement in line with the official framing of Heritage Day, not a factual claim that can be false.

items.bewering: Erfenis is tasbaar as jy dit kan sien en aanraak. Dit kan 'n plek, gebou of voorwerp wees.
items.bron: UNESCO, World Heritage Convention: cultural heritage means monuments, groups of buildings and sites (informea.org, Convention text, Art. 1); the usual contrast with intangible heritage sets buildings, historic places, monuments and artifacts as physical cultural property (Wikipedia, 'Intangible cultural heritage', summarising UNESCO).

items.bewering: Musiek, feeste en jou gesin se stories is nie-tasbaar. Jy kan dit nie aanraak nie.
items.bron: UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, Art. 2.2 (ich.unesco.org, 'What is intangible heritage'): its domains include oral traditions and expressions (stories), performing arts (music), and social practices, rituals and festive events (festivals).

items.bewering: UNESCO erken plekke wat vir die hele mensdom waardevol is, as wêrelderfenisterreine.
items.bron: whc.unesco.org: properties are inscribed for 'Outstanding Universal Value', meaning significance 'so exceptional as to transcend national boundaries and to be of common importance for present and future generations of all humanity'. Strictly, the World Heritage Committee inscribes sites under the UNESCO Convention, but saying UNESCO recognises them is the standard simplification.

items.bewering: So 'n plek moet vir toekomstige geslagte bewaar word.
items.bron: World Heritage Convention (1972): states undertake to 'identify, protect, conserve, present and transmit to future generations' the heritage on the list (whc.unesco.org, Understanding World Heritage; informea.org Convention text, Art. 4).

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het 12 van hierdie plekke.
items.bron: Current as of November 2026. Wikipedia, 'List of World Heritage Sites in South Africa' (last edited 10 November 2026): 12 (7 cultural, 4 natural, 1 mixed), with the latest two inscribed in 2024 (Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites, Pleistocene Occupation Sites). SA Tourism (southafrica.net): 'South Africa has twelve World Heritage Sites'. Travelnews.co.za, 29 July 2024, reported the 2024 inscriptions. No South African site was among the four African inscriptions at the 48th session, Busan, July 2026 (travelnoire.com: Comoros, São Tomé and Príncipe, Tunisia, South Sudan). The 2025 changes were an extension of iSimangaliso into Mozambique and a boundary change to the Cape Floral Region, neither of them a new site. Wikipedia reports that South Africa has nothing on its Tentative List. The count will change if a site is added, so check it again before any reprint.

items.bewering: Die Victoria-waterval in Zambië en Zimbabwe is natuurlik
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage List, 'Mosi-oa-Tunya / Victoria Falls' (whc.unesco.org/en/list/509; IUCN World Heritage Outlook, node 1037): a transboundary natural property of Zambia and Zimbabwe, inscribed in 1989 under natural criteria (vii) and (viii).

items.bewering: Die Victoria-waterval ... is natuurlik, want die natuur het dit gevorm.
items.bron: The reason given is a classification rule, and a learner will apply it to other sites. UNESCO does not list a site as natural because nature formed it. It lists it because its natural value is outstanding: scenery, landforms and geological history, or plants and animals (World Heritage Convention, Art. 2; Victoria Falls criteria (vii) and (viii)). Many cultural sites were also formed by nature. Robben Island, in this same block, is a natural island and is cultural. The hill at Mapungubwe is a natural sandstone hill. The Cradle of Humankind caves, Pinnacle Point, Sibhudu and the ǂKhomani landscape were all formed by nature and are all cultural sites (Wikipedia, 'List of World Heritage Sites in South Africa'). A learner using 'nature formed it, so it is natural' will misclassify most of South Africa's 7 cultural sites. The reasons the block gives for Mapungubwe, Robben Island and the Drakensberg ('mooi berge') do hold, because each names what the site is valued for.
items.regstelling: Give Victoria Falls' category in terms of what it is valued for, not what made it: it is natural because it is recognised for the natural wonder itself, a huge waterfall and its deep gorges, and not for anything people did there. That sets up the contrast with Mapungubwe (valued for what people built and did) and makes the Drakensberg's 'both' hold.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe in Limpopo is kultureel, want mense het daar gewoon en gebou.
items.bron: UNESCO, 'Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape' (whc.unesco.org/en/list/1099; worldheritagesite.org id 1099): cultural property inscribed in 2003 under criteria (ii)-(v), in Limpopo. The nomination dossier describes the elite living on top of the hill and commoners on the terrace below, with stone-walled and built settlement remains.

items.bewering: Robbeneiland is ook kultureel, want dit laat ons dink aan belangrike mense en aan wat daar gebeur het.
items.bron: UNESCO decision on Robben Island (whc.unesco.org/en/list/916; whc.unesco.org/en/decisions/2633): cultural property inscribed in 1999 under criteria (iii) and (vi). Its buildings 'bear eloquent testimony to its sombre history' and 'symbolise the triumph of the human spirit, of freedom, and of democracy over oppression' (quoted by southafrica.net). Its association with people and events is the basis of criterion (vi).

items.bewering: Die Maloti-Drakensbergpark is gemeng, want dit het albei: mooi berge en ou rotskuns van die San.
items.bron: UNESCO, 'Maloti-Drakensberg Park' (whc.unesco.org/en/list/985; IUCN World Heritage Outlook, node 1114; kznparks.com): a mixed property inscribed in 2000 under cultural criteria (i) and (iii), for the rock paintings of the San who lived there for more than four millennia, and natural criteria (vii), for its scenery, and (x), for biodiversity. The site is shared with Lesotho (Sehlabathebe, added 2013), which the lesson does not need to say.

items.bewering: Sowat 800 jaar gelede het mense van die Mapungubwe-koninkryk voorwerpe van goud gemaak.
items.bron: University of Pretoria Museums object record on Google Arts & Culture ('Gold rhinoceros figure'): dated CE 1250-1290. Radiocarbon dates place the gold objects in the early 13th century, made locally by indigenous goldsmiths (ganoksin.com / Oddy, Gold Bulletin 1984, as summarised). Sources date the kingdom from c. 1075-1220 (Wikipedia) to c. 1220-1300; SAHO gives about 1200-1300. All of these put the gold about 730-810 years before 2026, so 'sowat 800' holds. The objects were made locally (UNESCO nomination; goldsmithing techniques described in Oddy 1984).

items.bewering: Die goud is op die heuwel gevind waar die koning gewoon het.
items.bron: University of Pretoria record (Google Arts & Culture): 'Fragments of the gold rhinoceros were found on the summit of Mapungubwe Hill ... in 1933', from the 'original gold grave' (M1 A620). UNESCO nomination dossier (whc.unesco.org document 151741, as quoted): 'on top of the hill, the elite rulers resided'; the last gold burial was 'most probably the king'. Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': the king and his court lived on the sandstone hill.

items.bewering: Die bekendste stuk is 'n renoster van dun goudplaatjies om 'n houtvorm.
items.bron: Superlative 'bekendste': SAHO, 'Mapungubwe' (sahistory.org.za/article/mapungubwe): 'The best known of these objects is the golden rhinoceros.' University of Pretoria Museums lists the gold rhino first among the collection's most iconic objects. Construction: UP record (Google Arts & Culture), 'made of several pieces of thin gold foil, which was originally nailed onto a wooden carving' whose 'wooden core has since decayed'. The lesson's 'om 'n houtvorm' says no more than that the wood was there, which is true. One scholarly view (Duffey 2012, Journal of African Archaeology) holds that the foil may have been an ornament on a carved wooden bowl rather than a stand-alone figure. That does not touch anything the lesson says.

items.bewering: Al hierdie goud is tasbare erfenis.
items.bron: Follows from the definition confirmed above: physical objects are tangible heritage. The objects are held as a national collection by the University of Pretoria Museums (up.ac.za, Mapungubwe Collection).

items.bewering: Dit is getuienis van knap vakmense en van leiers met groot mag.
items.bron: UNESCO nomination dossier, as quoted: gold objects in elite burials on the royal hill, with the hill as the exclusive domain of the ruling family. The goldsmithing techniques used (beaten foil, tiny gold tacks, wire, beads) are described in Oddy, Gold Bulletin 1984 (dx.doi.org/10.1007/BF03214702), via ganoksin.com. Sacred leadership and class distinction at Mapungubwe: Huffman, quoted in Mail & Guardian, 15 June 1995, 'South Africa's golden Iron Age'.

items.bewering: Erfenis wat jy kan sien en aanraak, soos plekke, geboue en voorwerpe.
items.bron: As for 'Tasbaar of nie-tasbaar': World Heritage Convention Art. 1 (monuments, buildings, sites), and the UNESCO contrast of physical cultural property with intangible heritage. The entry is true read on its own.

items.bewering: Erfenis wat jy nie kan aanraak nie, soos musiek, feeste en tradisies.
items.bron: UNESCO 2003 Convention, Art. 2.2 (ich.unesco.org): performing arts, social practices, rituals and festive events, and traditions are intangible cultural heritage. The entry is true read on its own.

items.bewering: Die Verenigde Nasies se Organisasie vir Onderwys, Wetenskap en Kultuur, wat wêrelderfenisterreine erken.
items.bron: UNESCO's name is 'United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization' (interacademies.org; un.org), and the lesson's rendering matches it element for element. Afrikaans Wikipedia (af.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO) gives the form 'Opvoedkundige, Wetenskaplike en Kulturele Organisasie van die Verenigde Nasies'. Both are faithful translations, and choosing between them is a matter of language, not fact. UNESCO's role in World Heritage is under the 1972 Convention.

items.bewering: 'n Plek wat UNESCO erken omdat dit vir die hele mensdom waardevol is.
items.bron: whc.unesco.org: Outstanding Universal Value is significance 'of common importance for present and future generations of all humanity'. The entry is true read on its own.

items.bewering: Wat 'n bron vir ons wys oor wat in die verlede gebeur het.
items.bron: Faculty of History, University of Cambridge, 'Getting started: Reading primary sources' (hist.cam.ac.uk): sources become historical evidence when they are interpreted to make sense of the past. Canadian Museum of History, 'Think like a historian': primary sources provide direct evidence about the past. The simplification is acceptable for Grade 5 and the entry is true read on its own.

opsomming: Every count, date, place, classification and the one superlative checks out: South Africa still has 12 World Heritage Sites as of November 2026, since no South African site was added in 2025 or at the July 2026 session. One thing needs fixing: the lesson says Victoria Falls is natural 'because nature formed it'. Learners will use that as the rule for 'natural', and it is wrong, because Robben Island, the hill at Mapungubwe and most of South Africa's cultural sites were also formed by nature. The category should be explained by what the site is valued for.
